asr.full_text: How to register and fund your Mirror Trading International account. You will need the referral link of the person who invited you to join Mirror Trading International. It will look something like this. Click on that link, and you will be taken to the mymticlub.com website. Now click on the become a member button, and you will be taken to the registration screen. Your sponsor's username will be displayed in the sponsor information section. Next you will need to check whether you need to select the left or right-hand position. You will need to confirm this with your sponsor. Enter a username, the system will tell you if the username is available and the password. Fill in your personal information, your name, surname, email address, a valid mobile number and then choose your country from the drop down list. Once you have done this click on the register button. A screen will come up with a confirmation message which will confirm your login details. You will also receive an email from Meirio Trading International confirming your registration registration if you found this email in your spam folder you can inform your system that it is not spam and you'll be able to receive other emails from the company now that you have your login details please login to the back office at myMTIclub.com then click on the profile button to upload your proof of address. Once you have done this, you can click the updated button. Adding funds to your MTIP account Click the wallet menu on the left A roll down will appear Click on add funds The payment information screen will appear You can either scan the QR code or carefully copy the bitcoin address to your wallet Make the payment by sending the bitcoin Remember some wallets require you to verify the payment via email Fill in the details The amount of bitcoin you sent Enter the Blockchain Transaction ID and upload the amount of Bitcoin you sent and enter the Blockchain transaction ID and upload the proof of payment screenshot, then click Submit. Once the admin has received your Bitcoin it will appear in your trading account. However in some circumstances your balance may be in the Activation wallet. Only if your Bitcoin is in your Activation wallet, then click on the Pool account in the menu on the left and the roll roll-down, and click Add funds to Pool. Enter the amount of Bitcoin you want to transfer from your Activation Wallet to your trading account, and click Submit. Go back to your Dashboard and confirm that your Bitcoin is now in the trading account. Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades. You can also login to your back office to see the results and your statements. Click on the View option to see your daily statement. That is your account and how to see the results from daily trading. Should you wish to refer your friends, you can send them your registration link or you can help them to register by clicking on the down-lined registration link. For more information, please contact the person who sent you this video.

textual.context: Promotional and instructional context; the source presents the opportunity and registration process, but the speaker's specific relationship to the program is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised passive-income opportunity is linked to joining through a referral and funding a trading account, creating a reward/action relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: No specific income amount, timeframe, guarantee, eligibility terms, or outcome is established. These records do not establish whether the opportunity or organization is legitimate.

textual.observation: Viewers are instructed to send Bitcoin to fund a trading account, enter the transaction details, and upload proof of payment before the funds appear in the account.

textual.context: Presented as an account-funding tutorial. The records do not identify the recipient wallet owner or independently verify the transaction process.
textual.potential_relevance: A cryptocurrency transfer and payment-verification submission are required to fund an account presented for daily trading, linking a requested asset transfer and proof-of-payment step to the advertised trading activity.
textual.limitations: No actual transfer, loss, recipient identity, wallet ownership, or transaction outcome is established. The QR code and Bitcoin address themselves are not independently verified.

textual.observation: Registration requires viewers to submit personal contact information and later upload proof of address to the trading platform account.

textual.context: Instructional registration context; the stated purpose of the requested information is account creation and profile completion.
textual.potential_relevance: Personal contact details and proof of address are requested as steps to obtain access to the account that the source presents as a passive-income and trading opportunity.
textual.limitations: The records do not specify the information's handling, whether it is mandatory in practice, or whether any misuse or harm occurred.

visual.observation: The video presents a Mirror Trading International account registration flow that asks for a username, password, first and last name, email address, mobile number, country, and acceptance of terms, followed by a separate account-funding step.
visual.context: The screens are shown as a registration and funding tutorial for the displayed Mirror Trading International service; the supplied frames do not establish whether the service is legitimate or fraudulent.
visual.potential_relevance: Account creation and submission of personal information are linked to joining an investment-related service and proceeding to funding, which may merit review as a combined data-and-payment onboarding flow.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not show who receives the information, whether the form was actually submitted, or what happened after registration.

visual.observation: A back-office payment screen directs the user to select a BTC wallet address, enter a Bitcoin amount, paste a transaction ID or TXID, upload proof of payment, and submit; a Bitcoin QR code and wallet address are displayed.
visual.context: The screen is presented within the same Mirror Trading International back-office interface and appears to be a funding confirmation workflow.
visual.potential_relevance: A requested cryptocurrency transfer is tied to submitting transaction identifiers and proof of payment to activate or fund the account, creating a concrete payment-and-verification relationship for review.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish whether any transfer occurred, the recipient's identity, the value of the displayed address, or the result of submission.

visual.observation: The dashboard displays an 'Activation Wallet Balance' and a 'Trading Pool Balance' with BTC and USD amounts, while the account is labeled 'Free Member'; a later dashboard sample shows a nonzero trading pool balance and a zero activation wallet balance.
visual.context: These balances are shown as dashboard account fields; the frames do not explain the eligibility rules or whether the amounts are withdrawable.
visual.potential_relevance: The account funding flow is followed by displayed activation and trading-pool balances, linking payment/account activation with stated monetary account outcomes that may merit review.
visual.limitations: The samples do not establish that the balances represent actual funds, guaranteed returns, successful withdrawals, or financial loss.

visual.observation: The trading bonus report lists multiple transactions with percentage-labeled 'Trading Result' entries, marks them 'Paid,' and shows a total trading-bonus amount in BTC.
visual.context: The report is shown inside the service's back-office interface as an account statement or bonus report.
visual.potential_relevance: The displayed percentage results and paid BTC bonus total are concrete return-related claims associated with the account activity and funding workflow, which may merit review.
visual.limitations: The sampled report does not show the underlying trades, funding requirement, calculation method, or whether the listed payments were actually received.

visual_context_notes.observation: The material is presented as a branded instructional or promotional walkthrough, beginning with 'How to Register and fund your MTI Account' and showing the Mirror Trading International logo and website interface.
The video includes a prompt to contact the person who sent the video, without showing the person's identity or the communication channel.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it actively instructs viewers to join and fund a purported passive-income trading program through a referral link and Bitcoin payment, while presenting account balances and recurring trading bonuses as evidence of returns. It also directs viewers to choose a sponsor-linked left or right position and later refer friends, making participation dependent on a recruitment structure rather than merely explaining financial concepts.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S03 fits because the video promotes funding a managed trading account and links that participation to passive income and recurring trading returns. S06 is separately supported by the sponsor, left/right placement, team, direct-referral, binary-bonus, and downline-registration mechanisms shown and described.
